summary: ​Hey Juke bridges the gap between Earth science data and immersive auditory art. By pairing NASA Earth Information Centre visuals with custom soundscapes, we create immersive and interactive auditory experiences of three distinct datasets.
details:
Hey Juke is a gallery of a sonification of three distinct datasets including Sea Surface Currents and Temperature, DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide Level, GISTEMP v4 Global Temperature. Based on the datasets, we map each distinct parameters to a sound feature to compose a musical audio. By translating sight to sound, it makes the data analysis accessible to low-vision users and provide another method for data analysis. We specifically chose datasets related to the Earth temperature to raise awareness on global warming and climate change.

Various SI such as Claude, ChatGPT & Gemini were used to write the code producing the final visuals. Python was the primary programming language used for computer vision methods such as optical flow, and HTML was used to produce the interactive sonified data. Wix was used to build the website, where the Github-hosted interactive site was embedded.

The Earth has always been speaking. We just never learned to listen. Our project try to make an attempt to have her heard. We picked very real and significant observable features within the data to have it go through this “sonification” process. We built a jukebox for the planet, where each track is a different voice of the same Earth. One is the restless swirl of ocean currents, one is the rising weight of CO2 emissions, and one is the slow fever of global temperature. Press play, and you can hear the ocean breathe, the air thickens and the world warm. Every sound speaks for one observable quantity within the data which speaks volume. We hope the listener leaves with more than information. We hope they leave with the sense that the planet is a living thing, and that its changes are worth listening to.
